blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

items.t: Nearest rapid-transit station: Mission City Station (West Coast Express), 33200 North Railway Ave, Mission; TransLink states weekday trains run between Mission City and downtown Vancouver in morning and evening rush hours.
Bus exchange: Mission City Station, the loop terminus on BC Transit Route 34.
Route 34 East Side, BC Transit: Mission City Station via Heritage Park Centre to Dewdney Trunk Rd at Stave Lake St, the timing point toward this area.
Rolley Lake Park (BC Parks): 23 km northwest of Mission via Dewdney Trunk Road and Bell Street; 64 campsites, swimming, fishing and canoeing on the lake.
Hayward Reservoir Trail: Hayward Lake Reservoir, part of BC Hydro's Stave River project, with Reservoir Trail (east side) and Railway Trail (west side).

Stave Falls is a rural community inside the City of Mission, around the Stave River below Stave Lake — unlike Dewdney, Deroche and Lake Errock to the east, City of Mission bylaws apply here. The City's Rural Mission Strategy names Stave Falls first: "From Stave Falls, Steelhead and Silverdale to our other rural neighbourhoods"
The community centres on Dewdney Trunk Road, Wilson Street and Brackley Avenue, with the Powerhouse at Stave Falls at 31338 Dewdney Trunk Road
Stave Falls Elementary, 30204 Brackley Avenue, is the in-community school building the City used for the Rural Mission Strategy open house on October 7, 2025

The setting is a working hydro reservoir system, not a natural lakefront: BC Hydro describes water stored in Alouette Lake running into Stave Lake, through the Stave Falls powerhouse into Hayward Lake, then through Ruskin Dam to the Fraser River

blocks.text: Stave Falls: rules that affect buyers

items.t: City of Mission planning governs Stave Falls, under the new Official Community Plan adopted in 2025 as Bylaw 6350-2025, with a replacement Bylaw 6405-2026 put to public hearing on April 7, 2026 to formally add the Regional Context Statement

Mission updated Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020 on July 17, 2024 to incorporate provincial small-scale multi-unit housing in urban residential zones, under Bylaw 6299-2024-5949(163); rural Stave Falls lots are outside those urban zones
All secondary suites inside the City must be registered with the City, a suite must be a self-contained living space in a single-family home, and suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhouses

blocks.text: Stave Falls: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Rolley Lake Park's campground grew in 2026: the Province states 32 new drive-in sites opened in May 2026, bringing drive-in sites to 92, in a $4-million project with electrical and wastewater upgrades
BC Hydro lists the Stave Lake boat launch, Hayward Lake Reservoir Recreation Area and Ruskin Dam Recreation Area as the recreation sites beside the Powerhouse on Dewdney Trunk Road
Stave West has over 200 campsites across four campgrounds managed by Recreation Sites and Trails BC, including Kearsley Creek with equestrian corrals and Rock Creek for recreational-vehicle groups
Hayward Lake gets busy in summer with swimmers and paddlers, per BC Hydro, which is the seasonal traffic pattern on Dewdney Trunk Road past Wilson Street

blocks.text: Stave Falls: development and new projects

items.t: Rolley Lake Park campground expansion, Rolley Lake: 32 new drive-in campsites, completed May 2026, with reservations required from July 1, 2026; a provincial project, status read on the Province's release on 2026-11-03

Rural Mission Strategy, City of Mission: draft strategy for Stave Falls, Steelhead, Silverdale and other rural neighbourhoods, with public engagement in September–October 2025 and presentation to Council for adoption in November 2025 on the City's timeline, status read on 2026-11-03
The West Coast Express runs from Mission City Station in central Mission, five weekday westbound trains with no weekend service, per the TransLink timetable

blocks.text: Stave Falls: risks and due diligence

items.t: Treat every waterfront, dock and moorage claim as a title and BC Hydro check, because the shoreline is a working reservoir system running Alouette Lake to Stave Lake to Hayward Lake to Ruskin Dam
Check Agricultural Land Reserve status by parcel identifier number (PID) on the Agricultural Land Commission maps before assuming a second home is possible on a rural lot
